title: fix(turning)!: part off with the whole kerf behind the part's end face
body:
**Breaking post output: the posted Z of each existing part-off moves by half a blade width toward the bar.** For example: end face Z-70, 3 mm blade, orientation 2: the old program has `G01 X0 Z-71.5`, the new program has `G01 X0. Z-73.`.

## After the third read (head 6b845e5ef)

- **A. The free end is read on the part's own axis.** The door of 6c18258d1 tested document +Z. A model drawn lying down (along X) is stood up with TURN, so document Z is horizontal in OP10 and in an OP20 flip alike, and the flip passed. Now:
  - The kept side matters only when the model goes on past the plane on both sides (`parting_law::plane_inside_model`). At an end of the model, the model is the part, so any setup generates.
  - There, the Part arm refuses with `setup_align::part_off_problem`. It fits the part's own turning axis on the setup-frame facets (`multiaxis::axis::fit`) and reads it back into the document frame.
  - The sign: the as-modelled setup (no alignment) holds document +Z up the spindle.
  - A part modelled standing must point its document-up end up the spindle by 0.5 or more. At -0.5 or less it is "end for end". Between the two it is "no clear hold". There is no decision at 0.
  - A part modelled lying down has no as-modelled hold, so the setup cannot say which end is free: refused.
- **B. Saved projects.** The Part stamp has the salt `part-off-kerf-side-v1`, so a part-off saved before this PR loads Stale. The post refuses it until it is generated again. The other blade kinds keep their stamps.
- **Behaviour that worked on main and is refused now.** A part-off with the plane inside the model is refused in these setups:
  - an aligned setup that does not hold the part as modelled (for example the OP20 flip);
  - a setup with a part that is modelled lying down. `setup_align_lathe.rs` loses its PT1 for this reason.

  #3469 (a parameter for the side to keep) is the way back.

| case | main | 6c18258d1 | 6b845e5ef |
|---|---|---|---|
| X-drawn pin under TURN, plane at its end | Z-71.5 | Z-73 | Z-73 |
| X-drawn stubbed pin, plane inside, under TURN and TURN [-90,0,90] | generates | **generates, no refusal** | refused by name |
| Z-drawn stubbed pin, spin [0,0,90] about the spindle | Z-71.5 | Z-73 | Z-73 |
| saved part-off (fixture recorded on main), after load | Ok, posts Z-71.5 | **Ok, posts Z-71.5** | Stale, the post is refused; generated again it posts Z-73 |

## After the two re-reads (heads 9dadc2efd and 6c18258d1)

1. First re-read (blocker): a plane inside the model took its scrap side from the stock overhang. A model with its grip stub (Z-84..0, plane Z-70) under a stock with a 0.1 mm front facing allowance parted Z-70..-67, 3 mm into the part. Fix: the scrap side is the chuck side (`parting_law::chuck_side`), never a guess from the stock. No setup or machine field names the spindle that holds the bar, so the chuck is at lower Z (ISO 841). A plane with the whole model on the chuck side is refused by name. `part_kerf_refusal` reads the side by itself, not from the kernel.
2. Second re-read (blocker): the setup alignment is baked into the facets. In an OP20 flip setup the chuck holds the finished part, and the free end is scrap. Fix: `collect_job` refuses a Part op when `setup_align::reverses_axis` holds. The predicate is: the alignment turns document +Z to a negative setup Z. It covers each reversal of the turning axis, not only the flip preset. Refusal text: "a part-off cannot run in this setup: the setup holds the part end for end, so the chuck holds the finished part and the free end is the piece the blade would cut off as the part. The side to keep cannot be chosen yet - part off in a setup that holds the bar as modelled, or face the free end to length instead".
3. The note `CHUCK_NOTE` is now in plain words. It goes on the path only where the rule decides what is kept, that is, when the model is on both sides of the plane.

Hand trace (plane Z-70, 3 mm blade, orientation 2): path centre Z-71.5, posted Z-73, blade span Z-73..-70.

Red, then green readings:

| case | 6a82e57e9 | 9dadc2efd | 6c18258d1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| (c) issue case, plane at the model end | Z-73..-70 | Z-73..-70 | Z-73..-70 |
| (a) stub model, stock flush at the front | Z-73..-70 | Z-73..-70 | Z-73..-70 |
| (b) stub model, 0.1 / 1 / 5 mm front allowance | **Z-70..-67** | Z-73..-70 | Z-73..-70 |
| flip setup, stub model, plane Z-14 | - | **generates, no refusal** | refused by name |

The readings of 6a82e57e9 come from a scratch test on the API of that head. The test was not committed.

## Cause

The Part operation used its parting plane (Bottom Z) as the centre line of the blade. The kernel set the CL at `station_of(parting_z)` and the band at ± w/2 (`crates/motion/src/turning/parting.rs`, old lines 66-69). The #641 shift then posts the corner of the blade. For the end face Z-70 of #3452, the kerf was Z-71.5..-68.5. It removed 1.5 mm and the back chamfer of the finished part. Nothing caught it:

- The refusal "nothing to part" compared the kerf with the model silhouette only. Thus it refused the correct kerf beside the part end.
- The revolved-blade scan reads a through-axis kerf as scrap by design. Thus it was silent.
- `verify` does not judge turning.

## What changed

- **The kerf side** (`crates/motion/src/turning/parting_law.rs`, new). The plane is the end face of the finished part. The whole kerf is on the chuck side (lower Z), and one flank is on the plane. The CL is half a blade from the plane. A plane with the whole model on the chuck side is refused: `nothing to part - the model (Z0.000 to Z70.000) stands wholly on the chuck side (lower Z) of the parting plane Z70.000; the part is what stands above the plane, away from the chuck`. A part held from +Z (a sub-spindle, a mirrored setup) cannot be stated yet: #3469.
- **The flipped setup** (`crates/app/src/operation/job.rs`, `crates/app/src/setup_align.rs`): see "After the two re-reads", point 2.
- **The refusal** (`parting.rs`). It compares the kerf with the bar: the model span plus the two ends of the stock. It accepts the correct kerf past the end of the part when the bar continues. If the kerf does not touch the bar, it refuses and gives the values. Example: `nothing to part - the 3.000 mm kerf beside the parting plane (Z-73.000 to Z-70.000) does not meet the bar (Z-70.000 to Z0.000); set the setup's stock if the bar runs on past the part`. `StockEnv` gets `s_bot` (the near end of the bar), and `turning_stock::read` fills it.
- **The generation verdict** (`part_kerf_refusal`, called in the Part arm of `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`). A part-off path is refused (`GenError`, so it is never posted) if a cutting move puts the band of the blade into material of the finished part by more than 1 µm. The band is the width of the blade, never wider. Example: `the part-off cuts into the finished part: move 0 puts the 3.000 mm blade at Z-71.500 to Z-68.500, 1.500 mm past the part's end face at Z-70.000 - the whole kerf must stand on the chuck side (lower Z) of that face`. It reads the side from the chuck alone, so a kerf put on the wrong side for any reason is caught. It cannot prove the intent of the user when the model is on both sides of the plane. There the path says which rule it used (`CHUCK_NOTE`).
- **The other blade kinds.** Groove Rough and Groove Finish do not have this fault. Their kerf stays inside the groove window by construction: `crates/motion/src/turning/blade.rs:170-171` `let lo_c = if s_lo <= d_lo { s_lo } else { s_lo + half }; let hi_c = if s_hi >= d_hi { s_hi } else { s_hi - half };`. The new law runs only for Part, so it cannot refuse a legal groove. Relief and face groove are not separate kinds (`params.rs`). Threading and Form Turning are not blade cuts (`posting_nose::is_blade_cut`). Their goldens do not change.
- The decision record: `docs/decisions/3452-part-off-kerf-side.md`.

## The case of the issue, posted (orientation 2, 3 mm blade, end face Z-70)

| before (main) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|
| CL Z-70, kerf Z-71.5..-68.5 | CL Z-71.5, kerf Z-73..-70 |
| `G01 X30 Z-71.5` ... `G01 X0 Z-71.5` | `G01 X30 Z-73.` ... `G01 X0. Z-73.` |
| part 68.5 mm, chamfer removed | part 70 mm, chamfer kept |

With orientation 1 (+Z corner) the same kerf posts Z-70 (on the face). On main it posted Z-68.5, which is the RED output of `the_plus_z_corner_posts_the_end_face_itself`.

Golden `groove_part.nc` (fanuc-lathe, plane Z-10, 3 mm blade, orientation 2):

```
before                       after
(PART LOAD ADVANCE 30)       (PART LOAD ADVANCE 30)
G00 X12.1 Z-11.5             G00 X12.1 Z-13.
G01 X11. Z-11.5 F0.03        G01 X11. Z-13. F0.03
...                          ...
G01 X0. Z-11.5 F0.03         G01 X0. Z-13. F0.03
```

## Tests (red on main, then green)

- `crates/app/tests/lathe_part_off_kerf.rs` (new; it uses only the API of main, and was run on main with the fix stashed):
  - `a_part_off_at_the_end_face_keeps_the_whole_part`: RED on main `the kerf Z-71.5..Z-68.5 enters the part past its end face Z-70`. GREEN: each posted feed is at Z-73, and the part is 70 mm long.
  - `the_plus_z_corner_posts_the_end_face_itself`: RED on main `the +Z corner posts Z-70: [-68.5, ...]`. GREEN.
  - `a_flipped_setup_refuses_the_part_off_by_name`: RED on 9dadc2efd (`the part-off is refused: ()`). GREEN: the stubbed model in the flip setup is refused by name. The flipped part-only pin, parted at its +Z end, is refused by `no_part_past_plane`.
  - `a_setup_as_modelled_parts_the_stubbed_pin_behind_the_end_face`: the stubbed pin, plane Z-70 inside the model, posts Z-73, as modelled and with a spin about the spindle.
  - `a_part_modelled_lying_down_parts_only_at_its_end`: RED on 6c18258d1 (the lying stub generated). GREEN: the lying pin under TURN posts Z-73. The lying stub is refused under TURN and under TURN [-90,0,90].
- `crates/app/tests/part_off_saved_before_3452.rs` (new) with `crates/app/tests/fixtures/part_off_pre_3452.camproj`. The fixture was recorded on main 6679b1b4b by the env-gated `record_the_pre_3452_fixture`. `a_part_off_saved_before_3452_loads_stale_and_does_not_post` is RED on main and on 6c18258d1 (`left: Ok, right: Stale`). GREEN: the fixture holds the old CL Z-70. After load P1 is Stale and G1 (a groove finish) is Ok. The post is refused with `P1: inputs moved since generation`. Generated again, P1 has CL Z-71.5 and posts.
- `crates/motion/tests/turning_part_kerf.rs` (new; it uses the new API, so on main it does not compile):
  - `the_issue_case_kerf_stands_behind_the_end_face`: Ø30 pin Z-70..0 with a 1 x 45° back chamfer, 3 mm blade, bar to Z-84. Each blade band is within Z-73..-70 ± 1 µm. The part keeps 70 mm. The verdict and the meridian scan are silent. No note (the plane is at the end of the model).
  - `a_front_facing_allowance_never_turns_the_kerf_into_the_part`: the stubbed model with front allowances 0, 0.1, 1 and 5 mm. The kerf is always Z-73..-70, and the path has the note.
  - `a_model_wholly_on_the_chuck_side_is_refused_by_name`: the mirrored pin Z0..70 with the plane at Z70 is refused by the kernel and by the verdict.
  - `a_plane_the_model_runs_past_parts_toward_the_chuck`: model Z-40..0, plane Z-20, no stock. The kerf is Z-23..-20.
  - `a_kerf_that_meets_no_bar_is_refused_by_its_numbers`: refused with no stock and with a bar that ends at the face, accepted when the bar continues. The message gives the kerf and bar spans.
  - `the_verdict_refuses_a_kerf_into_the_part`: a hand-built plunge centred on the plane (the old output) is refused and the message gives 1.500 mm. 2 µm into the part is refused. A kerf put wholly on the part side (CL Z-68.5 on the stubbed model) is refused with "Z-70.000 to Z-67.000" and "3.000 mm past". A blade on the face or past it passes. A width of 0 or an empty model is refused (a judge that cannot measure never reports silence).

## Changed pins and goldens (old value -> new value, why)

All changes have the same cause: the CL moves from the plane to plane - w/2 (the waste side).

- `crates/app/tests/lathe_blade_corner.rs` `a_part_off_leaves_the_part_the_verified_kerf_leaves`: plane Z-20, 3 mm. Posted plunges for corners None/2, 1, 6: -21.5/-18.5/-20 -> -23/-20/-21.5. The back face of the part: -18.5 -> -20.
- `crates/app/tests/lathe_post.rs` `groove_and_part_post_to_the_lathe_golden`: `Z-11.5` -> `Z-13.`.
- `crates/app/tests/catalog_groove_part_off.rs`: `G01 X0 Z13.5` -> `Z12`. A new assertion is added: no part-off feed puts the blade above the end face Z15.
- `crates/app/tests/turning_blade.rs` `a_part_op_severs_the_bar_in_the_document`: CL z -10 -> -11.5.
- `crates/motion/tests/turning_blade.rs`:
  - `parting_ladders_to_the_axis_in_one_center`: centre station 0 -> -1 (2 mm blade).
  - `every_refusal_names_itself`: the plane z 50 is above the wall (top z 40). The text "off the end of the bar" -> "stands wholly on the chuck side", which is the refusal that now comes first.
- `crates/motion/tests/turning_stock.rs`, `turning_contour_stock.rs`: `StockEnv` literals get `s_bot: f64::NAN` (unknown, the same meaning as a non-finite `s_top`).
- Goldens:
  - `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/groove_part.nc`: 25 part-off lines Z-11.5 -> Z-13. Written with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` by its own test.
  - `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/groove_part.nc`: 25 lines Z-0.4528 -> Z-0.5118. Written by `lathe_post_inch`.
  - No other line changes.
- Catalog, regenerated by `cargo xtask catalog --case turning/groove-part-off` and `--case turning/cone-thread` (not edited by hand):
  - `groove-part-off.nc` and `cone-thread.nc`: part-off Z13.5 -> Z12. The X ladder is the same, X29 to X0 in 1 mm steps. The old program had one duplicate `G01 X0. Z13.5` (a float rung just above the axis). The new program does not have it.
  - At 6b845e5ef each `.camproj` changes in one more line: the stamp of the Part op (the salt). The stamps of the groove ops do not change.
  - The `.camproj` files are the tool's own rewrite, and the tool always writes the whole file. The catalog files were last written at project format 73, and main writes format 76. The rewrite gives new stamps and new cached paths for all operations. The posted `.nc` of each other operation is byte for byte the same; `example_catalog` regenerates and compares it. Thus the cache differences come from main changes after the last regeneration, not from this PR. The tool has no option to keep the diff smaller. The two review-fix commits change these files by 0 lines in total: the note line was added and then removed.
  - READMEs and the `build.camscript` comment now say the new Z values.

## Gate

The quick gate plan (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run`) has 717 steps, more than 80. Thus each touched binary was run alone (debug, `-j 6`), on the final head 6b845e5ef:

- motion: `--lib` 536 passed (10 ignored); `turning_part_kerf` 6; `turning_blade` 11; `turning_stock` 5; `turning_contour_stock` 4. All green.
- app: `lathe_part_off_kerf` 5; `part_off_saved_before_3452` 2; `lathe_blade_corner` 4; `catalog_groove_part_off` 1; `lathe_post` 7; `lathe_post_inch` 6; `turning_blade` 14; `setup_align_lathe` 4; `turning_stock_approach` 3; `drill_prior` 12; `coarse_laws` 6; `project_roundtrip` 76; `--lib -- part stamp` 31; `example_catalog` (filtered: groove-part-off and cone-thread regenerates and rebuilds, plus 2 contract tests) 6. All green.
- clippy `-D warnings`: `-p camcraft-motion --lib --tests` clean. `-p camcraft-app --lib` with the 8 touched test targets clean.

**Heavy lanes** (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6 cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main`, on the final head 6b845e5ef, release, `--ignored`): `wall 77.5 min, 244 step(s), 0 failed`.

- 1 heavy build (release `--no-run`), 37 motion heavy steps, 206 app heavy steps. All ok.
- The reached turning, lathe and setup lanes are all ok. They include:
  - `turning`, `turning_blade`, `turning_profile`, `turning_contour`, `turning_form`, `turning_bore`, `turning_bore_feeds`, `turning_thread`, `turning_thread_infeed`, `turning_holder`, `turning_holder_steel`, `turning_stock_approach`, `turning_axial_rapids`, `turning_insert_zone`, `turning_hidden_floor`;
  - `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_inch`, `lathe_post_tormach` (with its g30, g76_ladder, g76_start and thread lanes), `lathe_post_g76` (and schedule, sources), `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_post_thread_dips`, `lathe_post_turn_radius`, `lathe_chuck`, `lathe_cross_drill`, `lathe_cycle_exit`, `lathe_field_sim`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `lathe_workholding_kinds`, `lathe_workholding_live`, `sim_lathe_body`;
  - `setup_align_lathe`, `setup_align_mill_turn`, `setup_align_non_mill`, `example_catalog`, `project_roundtrip`.
- Known-fail steps, red as expected (not related to this PR):
  - motion #1950 `the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`;
  - motion #1950 `the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`;
  - app #1950 `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`;
  - app #2849 `fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`.

## Not exercised

- A real control or machine.
- Lathe posts other than `fanuc-lathe.cps` (mm and inch). The posting shim is the same for all of them, but these posts were not run: Tormach PathPilot Lathe (the post of the issue), LinuxCNC lathe, Haas lathe, Sinumerik lathe, and the mill-turn posts.
- The q03 project file of the issue (a QA artifact). Its geometry is rebuilt in the tests from the numbers in the issue.
- The UI (no application window was started).

`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` was already above the 400-line limit (about 4280 lines). This PR adds only 11 lines to its Part arm.

Follow-up (a parameter for the kerf position, default = this behaviour): #3469.

Effort: high (not escalated).

Changelog: Part (part-off) now puts the whole blade kerf on the bar side of the parting plane, which is the end face of the finished part. Before, the kerf was centred on the plane and cut half a blade width into the part (#3452). **Breaking:** the posted Z of existing part-off operations moves by half a blade width toward the bar. Example: end face Z-70, 3 mm blade, orientation 2: Z-71.5 becomes Z-73. A part-off whose kerf does not touch a known bar is refused and the message gives the values. A part-off path that cuts into the finished part is refused at generation. A part-off with the parting plane inside the model is refused in a setup that holds the part end for end, or when the part is modelled lying down, because the side to keep cannot be chosen yet. A part-off saved before this change must be generated again before it posts.

Fixes #3452
